:::: {.tk-cols}
::: {.tk-col}
Designing, controlling and assessing a fusion reactor means running plasma simulations
thousands of times. The physics codes that are accurate enough take hours per run. Neural
networks trained on those codes run in milliseconds, but a network returns an answer
for any input, including inputs far outside its training data.

**toktoit** is an integrated tokamak simulation in which any expensive physics module can be
swapped for a neural surrogate, but only behind a *guard*. At every radius and every time step
the surrogate has to show that it is inside the conditions it was trained on, that its
ensemble agrees with itself, and that its answer is physically possible. Where it can't, a
trusted physics model takes over, and the handover is recorded. The whole simulation is
written in JAX, so it compiles to one program and can be differentiated end to end, and it
speaks IMAS, the fusion community's standard data format, at every boundary.

The code is private for now. What is public is the argument: the method, the checks that
define "correct", every number with where it came from, and the mistakes.
[How this is built](about.qmd): the code is written by an AI agent, Claude, working to a
brief by a human owner who makes every physics, licence and publication decision.
:::

:::: {#tk-flow-notes}
::: {.tk-note data-node="m0"}
**M0 · Scaffold** (done 18 Sep 2026). Data structures for the plasma state, the guard, the
coupling loop, IMAS adapters, provenance records and a test suite, all checked on a toy physics
model before real physics was added.
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="torax"}
**TORAX backend.** TORAX, the open-source JAX transport code, wrapped as a backend. Reference
runs of the ITER hybrid scenario (5 s flat-top and 80 s current ramp-up), with output converted
to toktoit's data structures and provenance recorded. Entry 2.
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="newton"}
**Newton-Raphson coupling loop.** The nonlinear solve inside each time step uses Newton-Raphson,
with Picard iteration kept as a fallback. Entry 1.
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="fixed"}
**Fixed-step loop over TORAX.** toktoit's compiled fixed-step loop calls TORAX's own single
time step, so a run is one program and can be differentiated end to end. Compared against
TORAX's own driver in entry 3; solver stalls examined in entry 5.
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="guard"}
**QLKNN behind the guard.** QLKNN, a neural network trained on the QuaLiKiz turbulence code, runs
inside TORAX behind the guard. At each radius and time step where a check fails, a physics
model is used instead and the substitution is recorded. Entry 4.
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="rf"}
**Analytic RF heating.** TORAX's Gaussian RF heating model, wrapped with a typed entry point and
tests. Entry 5.
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="bal"}
**Energy and particle balance.** Each step's energy and particle balance rebuilt from TORAX's own
equations on the ramp-up benchmark; meets the agreed 10^-6^ per step ([OQ-5](/Blog/toktoit/decisions.qmd#oq-5)). Entry 8.
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="track"}
**Run tracking.** Every command that runs physics keeps a run record: settings, one record per
step, alerts and final status, optionally sent to a Simvue tracking server. Entry 9.
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="ascot"}
**ASCOT5 alpha heating into TORAX.** ASCOT5 follows each fusion alpha particle along its orbit;
the resulting heating replaces TORAX's local model. First cluster run done (entry 10). A second
run with ten times more markers awaits a decision ([OQ-11](/Blog/toktoit/decisions.qmd#oq-11)).
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="bench"}
**ITER benchmark: physics comparison.** Comparison against the published ITER hybrid profiles.
The wrapper check passes; the physics comparison is next, with the tolerance set at the
physicist review ([OQ-5](/Blog/toktoit/decisions.qmd#oq-5)).
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="fgs"}
**FreeGSNKE: MAST-U equilibrium.** FreeGSNKE, an open-source free-boundary equilibrium solver,
computes MAST-U plasma shapes from coil currents. Standalone: not yet coupled to transport.
Entry 6.
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="rev"}
**Physicist review (M1 gate).** A physicist reviews the benchmark, conservation and gradient
results and sets the benchmark tolerance. Not yet scheduled.
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="m2"}
**M2 · Training data.** Sampled datasets from first-principles turbulence codes, with
provenance. Not started.
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="m3"}
**M3 · Surrogates.** Neural-network ensembles with physics built in, running inside the loop
behind the guard. Not started.
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="fgst"}
**FreeGSNKE coupled to transport.** MAST-U equilibria feeding the transport loop. This needs a
transport model valid on a spherical tokamak, which QLKNN is not, so it follows M3.
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="m4"}
**M4 · Verification.** For each surrogate: proved properties, calibrated uncertainty and
closed-loop checks. Not started.
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="cert"}
**Certification review.** Human gate after M4: each surrogate is reviewed before it is used for
results. Not started.
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="m5"}
**M5 · Uncertainty and validation.** Uncertainty propagated through the coupled simulation, and
validation. Not started.
:::
::: {.tk-note data-node="sign"}
**Physicist sign-off.** The final human gate. Not started.
:::

```{=html}
<script>
/* Hover descriptions for the workflow flowchart. Quarto renders Mermaid after page load and
   does not bind Mermaid's own tooltips, so wait for the SVG, then match each node by its
   element id ("flowchart-<node>-<n>") to a .tk-note[data-node] block above. */
(function () {
  var tip = null;
  function show(html, x, y) {
    tip.innerHTML = html;
    tip.style.display = "block";
    var w = tip.offsetWidth, h = tip.offsetHeight;
    var left = Math.min(x + 14, window.innerWidth - w - 8);
    var top = y + 16 + h > window.innerHeight ? y - h - 12 : y + 16;
    tip.style.left = Math.max(8, left) + "px";
    tip.style.top = Math.max(8, top) + "px";
  }
  function hide() { if (tip) tip.style.display = "none"; }
  function bind() {
    var nodes = document.querySelectorAll(".tk-flow svg.mermaid-js g.node");
    if (!nodes.length) return false;
    var notes = {};
    document.querySelectorAll("#tk-flow-notes .tk-note").forEach(function (n) {
      notes[n.dataset.node] = n.innerHTML;
    });
    tip = document.createElement("div");
    tip.className = "tk-tip";
    tip.setAttribute("role", "tooltip");
    document.body.appendChild(tip);
    nodes.forEach(function (g) {
      var m = /flowchart-(.+)-\d+$/.exec(g.id);
      var html = m && notes[m[1]];
      if (!html) return;
      g.classList.add("tk-has-note");
      g.addEventListener("mousemove", function (e) { show(html, e.clientX, e.clientY); });
      g.addEventListener("mouseleave", hide);
      g.addEventListener("click", function (e) { e.stopPropagation(); show(html, e.clientX, e.clientY); });
    });
    document.addEventListener("click", hide);
    window.addEventListener("scroll", hide, { passive: true });
    return true;
  }
  window.addEventListener("load", function () {
    var tries = 0;
    var t = setInterval(function () { if (bind() || ++tries > 50) clearInterval(t); }, 200);
  });
})();
</script>
```

## Milestones

Each milestone has acceptance criteria fixed in advance; three of them end in a review by a
human expert, not by the agent that built the code.

| | milestone | what it delivers | state | human gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| M0 | [Scaffold](milestones/M0.qmd) | data structures, the guard, the coupling loop, IMAS adapters, tests | [done 18 Sep 2026]{.wf .done} | — |
| M1 | [Open baseline](milestones/M1.qmd) | open-source physics codes wired in; a published benchmark reproduced | [in progress]{.wf .wip} | [physicist review]{.wf .crit} |
| M2 | Training data | sampled datasets from first-principles turbulence codes, with provenance | [not started]{.wf .todo} | — |
| M3 | Surrogates | neural ensembles with physics built in, running inside the loop | [not started]{.wf .todo} | — |
| M4 | Verification | proved properties, calibrated uncertainty, closed-loop checks per surrogate | [not started]{.wf .todo} | [certification review]{.wf .todo} |
| M5 | Uncertainty and validation | uncertainty propagated through the coupled simulation; validation | [not started]{.wf .todo} | [physicist sign-off]{.wf .todo} |

## What's next

- **ASCOT5 alpha heating with enough markers.** The first cluster run (entry 10) connected
  ASCOT5 to TORAX and set the orbit tolerance. A second run, with ten times more markers and a
  tighter-tolerance check, is awaiting a decision ([OQ-11](/Blog/toktoit/decisions.qmd#oq-11)). The approach then extends to
  neutral-beam ions once the injector geometry is approved.
- **Run the physics benchmark.** Compare against the published profiles at the published
  settings, then at a converged time step, ahead of the physicist review that sets the
  tolerance ([OQ-5](/Blog/toktoit/decisions.qmd#oq-5)).
- **Future extension:** extending the benchmark to a STEP power-plant flat-top is planned as a
  future extension. For now the work stays with the ITER benchmark and MAST-U.
:::
